description.value: A PET study comparing resting cerebral glucose metabolism in patients with mild frontotemporal dementia and semantic dementia with healthy age-matched controls.

spans.text: The objective of the present study was to determine the pattern of cerebral glucose metabolism in FTD and SD in comparison with age-matched healthy subjects using 18F-FDG-PET.

model_settings.value: SPM99 two-sample t-test comparisons of FTD versus controls and SD versus controls; interindividual differences in tracer uptake were modeled using one-way ANOVA. Voxel-level uncorrected threshold P < 0.001, with multiple-comparison correction and interpretation restricted to P < 0.001 corrected.

spans.text: Data analysis included two steps. First, cerebral glucose metabolism was compared between FTD patients and controls (two-sample t -test). Interindividual differences in tracer uptake were included in the statistical model using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). Second, cerebral glucose metabolism was compared between SD patients and controls using the same statistical model.
For statistical analysis we used the SPM 99 software (Statistical Parametric Mapping; Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK).

description.value: 18F-FDG-PET data underwent transmission-scan attenuation correction and correction for random events, dead time, and scatter. Images were reconstructed by filtered back-projection, stereotactically normalized using NEUROSTAT, and smoothed with a 12 × 12 × 12 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel before SPM99 analysis.

spans.text: Data were corrected for random, dead time and scatter, and images were reconstructed by filtered back-projection with a Hamm filter (cut-off frequency 0.5 cycles/projection element) resulting in 47 slices in a 128×128 pixel matrix (pixel size 2.0 mm) and interplane separation of 3.447 mm.
